label: End of a 9-token original sequence: final token l, or <DEL> (very sparse, conjunctive)
explanation: Extremely sparse feature (0.002% of steps, ~260 sequences). Every activation is at the original/delimiter boundary, t=8 or t=9, almost all in L=9 sequences (86% of mass; the rest are L=8 delimiter steps). It fires either on the last original token when that token is l (42% of mass) or on the <DEL> step (54%). It never fires in the copy phase or earlier in the original phase. Whether it fires depends on what came before: it is strongly enriched when the first token is r (18x lift, 64% of mass; g and 2 are weaker), and when the token just before is d (16x lift, 54% of mass). The largest activations combine all three, e.g. r ... d l. The location predicate captures 82% of mass but has precision of only about 0.1%, because nearly all L=9 boundary steps are silent. Adding first-token and prev-token conditions raises precision only to about 6% and loses recall, so the exact trigger is a sparse conjunction that is not fully captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=r (+2.93), prev_tok=d (+2.48), t=8 & in_tok=l (+1.93), orig4=m (+1.73), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=l (+1.70), phase=0 & in_tok=l (+1.70). Lower it: next_out=- (-2.51), orig8=- (-2.41), orig7=- (-2.26), in_first=0 (-1.94).
